stations.description: New Orleans' listener-supported jazz and heritage station: brass bands, blues, R&B, zydeco, and the city's own DJs.

about.text: WWOZ is a non-profit community-supported radio station in New Orleans. It is owned by the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Foundation. The station specializes in music from or relating to the cultural heritage of New Orleans and the surrounding region of Louisiana. The playlist includes jazz, blues, local, regional and world music.

stations.name: WQXR
stations.description: New York's classical station, hosted all day, from the morning show to live concerts.

about.text: WQXR-FM is an American non-commercial classical radio station, licensed to Newark, New Jersey, and serving the North Jersey and New York City area. It is owned by the nonprofit organization New York Public Radio (NYPR), which also operates WNYC (AM), WNYC-FM and the four-station New Jersey Public Radio group. The station is the core audio service for NYPR's WQXR brand.

stations.name: New Sounds
stations.description: John Schaefer's New Sounds: new music from everywhere, ambient to avant-garde, chosen by hand in New York.

about.text: New Sounds is a radio program on WNYC that features contemporary and world music. Hosted by John Schaefer, the program has been running since 1982.

stations.name: KCSM Jazz 91
stations.description: The Bay Area's jazz station, listener-supported and hosted around the clock.

about.text: KCSM is an FM radio station in San Mateo, California. The station broadcasts jazz music, 24 hours a day, commercial-free. The radio station is not-for-profit, and listener-supported. The broadcast is mirrored as streaming media on the World Wide Web, extending the station's audience far beyond the San Francisco Bay Area.

stations.name: WFMT

about.text: WFMT is a commercial FM radio station in Chicago, Illinois, with a classical music radio format. It is part of Window to the World Communications, Inc, in the same company as Chicago's PBS member station WTTW.

stations.name: The Current
stations.description: Minnesota Public Radio's music station: indie, local bands, live sessions, hosted all day.

about.text: KCMP is a radio station owned by Minnesota Public Radio (MPR) that airs an adult album alternative (AAA) music format, including a significant rotation of songs by local artists.

stations.name: Classical California
stations.description: Los Angeles' classical station, the largest in the country, hosted live.

about.text: KUSC is a non-commercial radio station in Los Angeles, California, United States, broadcasting a classical music format. It is owned by the University of Southern California (USC) and is part of its Classical California network.

stations.name: WKCR
stations.description: Columbia University's station since 1941: deep jazz, classical, American roots and new music, programmed by students who know their archives.

about.text: WKCR-FM is a radio station licensed to New York, New York. The station is owned by Columbia University and serves the New York metropolitan area. Founded in 1941, the station traces its history back to 1908 with the first operations of the Columbia University Radio Club (CURC). In 1956, it became one of the first college radio stations to adopt FM broadcasting, which had been invented two decades earlier by Professor Edwin Howard Armstrong.

stations.name: WPRB
stations.description: Princeton's freeform college station: indie, experimental, jazz, whatever the DJ carried in.

about.text: WPRB is an FM radio station licensed to Princeton, New Jersey, and owned by Princeton Broadcasting Service, Inc. It broadcasts a freeform radio format, including shoegaze, slowcore, noise music, harsh noise wall, plunderphonics, illbient, jazz, electronic, folk, reggae, ska, metal, world, soul, rap, blues, screamo, and rock. While the station is non-profit, it is licensed as a commercial radio station. Much of the on-air staff and management are Princeton University alumni and students.

stations.name: KALX
stations.description: Berkeley's student-and-community station: freeform, deep, and allergic to playlists.

about.text: KALX is a radio station that broadcasts from the University of California, Berkeley in Berkeley, California, United States. The station employs three full-time paid staff members, but is largely run by its nearly 300 volunteers, including Berkeley students and other members of the local community.

stations.name: KFJC
stations.description: Foothill College's freeform station in the hills above Silicon Valley, strange and beloved since 1959.

about.text: KFJC is a student-run college and community radio station licensed to Foothill College in Los Altos Hills, California. The station, which has a Variety format, broadcasts a broad spectrum of musical genres as well as public affairs programming. KFJC serves the southern San Francisco Bay Area.

stations.name: KXLU

about.text: KXLU is a non-commercial, free-form, college and community radio station broadcasting out of Loyola Marymount University in southwest Los Angeles, California.

stations.name: WMBR

about.text: WMBR is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's student-run college radio station, licensed to Cambridge, Massachusetts, and broadcasting on 88.1 FM. Both students and community members can apply for positions, and like many college radio stations, WMBR offers diverse programming that includes a broad range of musical genres as well as talk shows.

about.text: WSOU is a non-commercial, student-run college radio station. The station broadcasts from the campus of Seton Hall University in South Orange, New Jersey.

about.text: Rinse FM is a London-based community radio station, licensed for "young people living and/or working within the central, east and south London areas". It plays garage, grime, dubstep, house, jungle, UK funky and other dance music genres popular in the United Kingdom.

stations.name: Soho Radio

about.text: Soho Radio is an independent radio station that broadcasts online from London and from New York, as well as on DAB in London. It was founded May 2014, with the New York branch opening in November 2020.

stations.name: Resonance FM
stations.description: London's art radio since 2002: sound art, improvised music, radio made by artists.

about.text: Resonance 104.4 FM is a London based non-profit community radio station specialising in the arts run by the London Musicians' Collective (LMC). The station has been called "the best radio station in London" by The Guardian and "the best radio station in the world" by The Village Voice. Resonance is operated by hundreds of volunteer technical and production staff.
